heroHeadline: Sandu Pledges Air-Defense Investment as EU Sets September 1 Retry on Stalled Accession Clusters
heroSubtitle: Two days after a five-drone overnight wave breached Moldovan airspace ahead of the country's 35th Independence Day, President Maia Sandu said on August 27 that Moldova is "investing in air defense to develop the capabilities needed to protect its population and critical infrastructure," while calling for closer Moldova-Ukraine-Romania threat-sharing — an acknowledgment that, as a neutral non-NATO state, Moldova currently cannot shoot down intruding drones itself. Separately, new reporting on August 28 detailed that two of the five August 27 drones vanished from radar while still over Moldovan territory, including one over the Transnistrian sector where Chisinau has no ground access to investigate. On the EU accession track, the Council's Working Party on Enlargement is set to resume work on September 1 to reconsider opening negotiation clusters 2 and 3 for Moldova and Ukraine, after Hungary blocked the same approval twice in July despite reportedly being willing to advance Moldova's cluster alone.
